claim: NLRB GC 23-02 was rescinded on 14 Feb 2025 by GC 25-05 (legal_privacy, confirmed: true)
problem: The cited URL (the 31 Oct 2022 NLRB news story on GC 23-02) never mentions rescission or GC 25-05. The fact is true - nlrb.gov's 'GC 25-05 Rescission of Certain General Counsel Memoranda' page is dated 14 February 2025 and lists GC 23-02 among the rescinded memos - but the brief's citation does not support it.
fix: Add https://www.nlrb.gov/news-outreach/news-story/gc-25-05-rescission-of-certain-general-counsel-memoranda as the source for the rescission sentence (keep the 2022 URL only for what GC 23-02 said).

claim: legal_privacy 'Records the client is legally obliged to keep': ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.6 requires retained documented information on acceptance criteria and authorizing person - cited to sp-i.org/downloads/spi-09.pdf
problem: SPI-09 is the AS9102 FAIR guidebook and contains no reference to ISO 9001 (searched: no match for '9001'). The clause text is correct, but the citation does not support it. The same fact is correctly cited elsewhere in the brief to the ISO 9001:2015 PDF.
fix: Cite https://ipc11.dip.go.th/.../2a5458cc6b38553834457b0f88607459.pdf (ISO 9001:2015, 8.6) for the clause; keep SPI-09 only for AS9102C.

claim: Overview.ai OV10i is classification-only on a 1.6 MP sensor with NVIDIA Xavier NX and no software subscription - cited to https://www.overview.ai/shop/
problem: The shop page lists only the OV80i (price, accessories); it carries no OV10i or OV20i specification. The claim is accurate, but only on the product page /products/ov10i/ (which states 'Algorithm Classification only', 1.6MP SONY IMX296, NVIDIA Xavier NX, 'No software key or subscription needed').
fix: Point the OV10i specs to https://www.overview.ai/products/ov10i/ and keep /shop/ only for the $13,450 OV80i price.

claim: Pilot cost: '$7,000-$18,000' from '50-100 engineering hours at $100-$150/hr' plus hardware $1,500-$5,000
problem: The stated inputs imply a wider band ($6,500 at the low end, $20,000 at the high end: 100 h x $150 + $5,000), so the quoted ceiling sits below what the assumptions produce. It is an internal arithmetic inconsistency in an estimate, not a sourced fact.
fix: Either widen the range to roughly $6,500-$20,000 or state that the top of the range assumes fewer hours / cheaper lighting than the stated maxima.
